p03_reverification.unknown_resolved_2026_09_18: The string-vs-numeric chain id unknown is CLOSED, from the documentation rather than from a live execution call: https://docs.keeperhub.com/api/direct-execution documents `chainId` as the numeric chain id, accepted as a number or a numeric string, with a deprecated `network` field for chain names. Held sends the numeric chainId, which is correct. The internal catalog string id is a listing identifier and is not what the execution route expects. NOT tested against the live execution route -- no contract call has been made on it.

layers.question: Does the pinned SDK know Base Sepolia?
layers.finding: The literal 84532 appears NOWHERE in the pinned repo. But chain IDs are not how the SDK selects a chain: it uses chain NAME ('base') crossed with a Network enum (MAINNET|TESTNET|SEPOLIA|ANVIL). TESTNET routes to SEPOLIA; ANVIL is is_local. rpc_provider builds Alchemy URLs as {chain_key}-sepolia..., so base+sepolia RESOLVES at the RPC layer.
layers.boundary: RPC resolution is not protocol support. See L6 - that is the decisive layer.

layers.question: Would chain=base + network=sepolia give correct Morpho addresses?
layers.finding: DECISIVE. MORPHO_BLUE, MORPHO_BLUE_TOKENS and MORPHO_MARKETS are all dict[chain_name][...] with NO Network awareness anywhere in addresses.py. So chain=base + network=sepolia would talk to a Base Sepolia RPC while returning BASE MAINNET singleton, token and market params. Those markets do not exist on Base Sepolia; compiled calldata would target wrong or codeless addresses.
layers.boundary: This rejects the SUPPORTED PROFILE on Base Sepolia. It does not reject a custom registry extension - but V4 forbids silently repointing the 'base' config at another chain, so any extension is a separate versioned decision.

layers.finding: The SDK has a first-class Network.ANVIL with is_local=True and per-chain local fork URLs (config/runtime.py:710,761). chain=base + Network.ANVIL forking Base MAINNET gives correct mainnet addresses AND local control. This is the correct vehicle for P00 item 6 and P02.

p03_status.still: Was 'BLOCKED-UNKNOWN. Unchanged. No org API key; nothing local closes this.' The first clause is superseded by m1_route_proof below; the second remains exactly true -- nothing local closes this.
p03_status.what_p03_built: The client that would exercise it: adapter/held_adapter/execution/keeperhub.py. preflight() is a SIMULATE-mode call on the authenticated route, so a 2xx there would be the first genuine evidence about L10 this project has.
p03_status.anti_simulation: Only HttpsTransport can produce hosted=True, and it requires an https:// origin with a real credential. OfflineTransport stamps hosted=False, and SendResult.assert_hosted_evidence() refuses a non-hosted result, so a local fixture cannot be filed as an L10 pass. 43 local tests cover request construction, execution keys, backoff, response classification and the credential check; none of them establish L10, and four exist specifically to prove they cannot.

m1_route_proof.what_ran: make check-l10-route-proof -> script/collect_route_proof.py. One authenticated GET https://app.keeperhub.com/api/keys over HttpsTransport. No broadcast, no deployment, no funds; the script has no code path that can submit a contract call.
m1_route_proof.observed: HTTP 200, hosted=true. The organisation lists one key; the configured secret matches it by the documented keyPrefix, so the 200 is attributable to THIS credential rather than to an endpoint that ignores the Authorization header. Scope reads 'mcp:read'. Role owner, no expiry.
m1_route_proof.why_this_is_the_first_hosted_result: Every prior KeeperHub result in this repository came from OfflineTransport and carried hosted=false. This is the first hosted=true one.
what_it_establishes: The live organisation route accepts Held's credential -- a fact no local test could produce, and one GET /api/chains could never produce either, since that route answers 200 with no credential at all.
The scopes actually attached to the credential.
what_it_does_NOT_establish: L10 itself. The question is whether the authenticated caller/payer accepts Held's OUTER CONTROLLER CALL. A credential listing says nothing about that, and answering it needs a simulate-mode contract call against a DEPLOYED HeldController. None is deployed on any public chain.
M1. M1 is a real transaction executed through KeeperHub. A credential listing is not a transaction.
m1_route_proof.hard_consequence: The scope is mcp:read. The documentation states a mcp:read key can read and simulate but cannot broadcast, and that broadcasting requires mcp:write or mcp:admin. So M1 is not merely unperformed on this credential -- it is unreachable on it. KeeperHubClient.assert_can_broadcast() now refuses a broadcast on an observed read-only scope BEFORE sending it, rather than discovering the documented 403 insufficient_scope afterwards.
m1_route_proof.chain_id_unknown_closed: The CHECKPOINT open unknown about the catalog's internal string chain id versus the numeric chainId is closed from the documentation, not from this call: https://docs.keeperhub.com/api/direct-execution documents chainId as the numeric id, as a number or a numeric string, with a deprecated `network` field for chain names. Held sends the numeric chainId, which is correct. This was NOT tested against the live execution route.
m1_route_proof.authenticated_response_schema_unknown: Still open for the EXECUTION route. The /api/keys response schema is now observed; the contract-call response schema is not.

layers.question: Can a pinned Base-mainnet fork actually run here?
layers.finding: YES. anvil 1.8.3 forks Base at block 51353212 and serves chain 8453 with real Morpho code and live market state. CONSTRAINT: on this device each shell call runs in its own network namespace with --die-with-parent, so a background anvil CANNOT survive between calls. The fork must start, be used and be torn down inside ONE invocation. fixtures/with_fork.sh does this and REFUSES to hand over a fork whose chain id, block or Morpho code does not match fixtures/fork.env.
layers.boundary: Self-tested. Not yet used for a full baseline scenario.
